close_reason: Typed CalendarEventGetArgs.recurrence_overrides_{before,after} as Option<UTCDate>. Handler validates via UTCDate::new_validated and rejects malformed input as invalidArguments at the handler boundary, matching the principal.rs:51-59 pattern. Two regression tests added covering both fields. PLAN.md and rustdoc updated. fmt/clippy/test/doc all green.
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:667 and :671 expose `pub recurrence_overrides_before: Option<String>` and `pub recurrence_overrides_after: Option<String>`. The rustdoc on each says the value is a UTCDateTime that the backend must compare against recurrence-id-translated-to-UTC values.

`jmap_types::UTCDate` already exists in the dep graph and IS used elsewhere in the same trait:
- line 351 (compute_utc_times return)
- lines 556-557 (get_availability `utc_start` / `utc_end`)
- The Principal/getAvailability handler at principal.rs:51-59 even uses `UTCDate::new_validated` to reject malformed values BEFORE the backend sees them.

Yet the same trait routes the structurally-identical recurrence_overrides_before/after through `Option<String>`. Every backend implementor is forced to re-parse on every CalendarEvent/get call, and a malformed UTCDateTime reaches the backend rather than being rejected as `invalidArguments` at the handler boundary (see event.rs:69-77 which just calls `.as_str().map(to_owned)`).

What callers cannot rely on:
- That the value reaching the backend is a syntactically-valid UTCDateTime.
- That two backend impls agree on what counts as valid.
- That a malformed string is the handler's fault to reject (no signal in the type).

The fix is to change the field type to `Option<UTCDate>` and have the handler validate via `UTCDate::new_validated` exactly as `principal.rs:51-59` does for `utcStart`/`utcEnd`. Non-breaking now (pre-1.0); SemVer-breaking later. Should land before the args struct stabilises.
title: CalendarEventGetArgs.recurrence_overrides_before/after: Option<String> instead of Option<UTCDate>
